##### **Step 1: Check out our test "Sandbox"**
To help developers get comfortable with the PitchBook API, a test "sandbox" environment has been created to show how API calls are structured and how to integrate them with your system. Please reach out to your account manager to request a sandbox key.

## Authentication
To authenticate to the PitchBook API, simply include a header named "Authorization" with the value of "PB-Token {API_KEY}" with each API request.
Replace {API_KEY} with your actual API key value.
In addition to an API key, please make sure you have purchased API credits. Each call has a defined cost. Reach out to your account manager to view and add credits to your API credit balance.
**Authentication Example**
> [https://api.pitchbook.com/{route}](https://api-v2.pitchbook.com/%7Broute%7D)
> Authorization: PB-Token LzUU9xgNjn7avDw5Bd96xNVS0t5dlGuD

PitchBook is a market intelligence platform providing a RESTful API for on-demand access to private and public market data such as companies, deals, investors, and funds. The REST API base URL is `https://api.pitchbook.com` and all requests require an Authorization header with a custom token format.

## How do I authenticate with the PitchBook API?
PitchBook authenticates requests using a static API key passed in the Authorization header with the format 'PB-Token {API_KEY}'.
**1. Get your credentials**
Access to the PitchBook API is a paid, contract-gated add-on and is not available via a self-serve dashboard. To obtain credentials: 1. Contact your PitchBook account manager or your organization's PitchBook administrator to request API access. 2. Once the add-on is enabled, your account manager will provision your API key. 3. Alternatively, you can log in to the PitchBook platform and navigate to 'My PitchBook' > 'Plugins & Apps' > 'PitchBook API' to reach out to the Direct Data team to initiate the request.
**2. Add them to `.dlt/secrets.toml`**
```
[sources.pitchbook_source]
api_key = "your_pb_token_here"
```
dlt reads this automatically at runtime — never hardcode tokens in your pipeline script. For production environments, see [setting up credentials with dlt](https://dlthub.com/docs/walkthroughs/add_credentials) for environment variable and vault-based options.

auth.title: PitchBook integration
auth.snippet:
PitchBook (a Morningstar company) is a market intelligence platform for private and public capital markets — companies, investors, funds, deals, people, limited partners, and service providers. Integrating PitchBook with Frontegg lets your application search and read this data on behalf of your users — all through Frontegg's integration layer (PitchBook Public API v2). PitchBook authenticates with a static API key sent on every request, so there is no OAuth flow.

PitchBook authenticates API requests with a static API key, sent on every request as the `Authorization: PB-Token <key>` header.
####
Step 1: Obtain your API key
PitchBook API keys are provisioned as part of a paid API add-on rather than generated self-serve. Contact your PitchBook account manager (or your organization's PitchBook administrator) to enable API access and issue an API key for your account.
PitchBook also offers a test **sandbox** environment that uses the same base URL with a separate key. If you want to try the integration before running against production data, ask your account manager for a sandbox key as well.
####
Keep your API key secure
The API key grants access to your PitchBook data through the API. Treat it like a password and never expose it in client-side code or commit it to version control. If it is exposed, ask PitchBook to rotate it.
###
Configure the Frontegg portal
Once you have your API key, configure the integration in the Frontegg portal:
1. Open the **Frontegg portal** and navigate to [ENVIRONMENT] → Integrations → PitchBook.
2. Paste your **API Key**.
3. Optionally set a **Default currency** — an ISO 4217 code (for example, `USD`, `EUR`, `GBP`, `JPY`) applied to all monetary fields in responses. Leave it blank to use PitchBook's default.
4. Click **Save**.
####
Keep your credentials secure
Never share or commit your API key to version control.

access.title: PitchBook API Review: Can You Build on It? [2026]
access.snippet:
The answer is complicated. PitchBook does offer a [RESTful JSON API](https://pitchbook.com/products/direct-access-data/api) covering all of its core entity types, but the API is an enterprise add-on that requires a separate contract on top of an existing platform subscription. The developer documentation is not publicly accessible. There are no published rate limits, no public endpoint reference, no official SDKs, and no self-serve signup.

| **Attribute** | **Detail** |
|---|---|
| **API type** | REST over HTTPS, JSON responses |
| **Authentication** | API key or token-based (specific mechanism not publicly documented) |
| **Base URL** | Not publicly documented |
| **Rate limits** | Not publicly documented |
| **Pricing / access** | Enterprise add-on requiring a [separate contract](https://pitchbook.com/help/PitchBook-api) on top of a PitchBook platform subscription; quote-only |
| **SDKs** | None |
| **Webhooks** | Not supported |
| **Documentation** | Behind platform authentication; not publicly accessible. [Help page overview](https://pitchbook.com/help/PitchBook-api) available |

Getting API access is not a self-serve process. The API belongs to **PitchBook's** [Direct Data](https://pitchbook.com/products/direct-access-data) product line, and access requires a [standalone contract](https://pitchbook.com/help/PitchBook-api) separate from a standard platform subscription. There is no developer portal, no API key generator in the dashboard, and no free-trial API access.

Developer support routes through the assigned account team and Direct Data specialists. There is no public developer forum, community channel, or self-serve support path.

**PitchBook** does not publish API or Data Feed pricing. Both are [premium add-ons](https://pitchbook.com/pricing) to the core platform subscription, and each requires a separate contract. The base PitchBook platform is required before Direct Data can be contracted, which means API access requires at minimum two separate agreements: the platform subscription and the Direct Data contract.
Cost varies by seat count and firm type; all Direct Data pricing is quote-only and negotiated through PitchBook's Direct Data team. No per-call metering, credit-pack costs, or minimum plan tiers appear anywhere on the public site. access.title: PitchBook API: Access, Pricing, and What You Get
access.snippet:
PitchBook doesn’t sell its API as a standalone product with a price tag. It’s a premium add-on layered on top of a paid platform subscription. Access only comes through a separate contract with PitchBook’s Direct Data team. There’s no public price list for it anywhere, not even on PitchBook’s own site. This guide walks through what it costs, what it actually gives you, and whether your team needs it.

There’s no developer signup page. There’s no “generate an API key” button in the dashboard. You can’t start testing without a sales conversation first. Access works differently depending on where you’re starting from:
- **Existing PitchBook platform customers** go to *My PitchBook → Plugins & Apps → PitchBook API* inside the platform. That routes a request to the Direct Data team.
- **New customers** contact the Direct Data team directly. API access then gets negotiated alongside a platform subscription.
Either way, credentials only arrive after a contract is signed — an API key or token. A sandbox environment exists for pre-production testing once you’re in the process. It gives developers a space to practice calls before

This is the part that catches developers off guard. It’s worth setting expectations before you sign anything:
- **No public rate limits.** Call-volume caps and burst limits aren’t published anywhere. Constraints get set per contract with the Direct Data team, so you can’t plan integration capacity until after the deal is signed.
- **No official SDKs.** The API works with any standard HTTP client, but no maintained client library exists in any language. Your team owns the full integration layer: authentication, request handling, pagination, retries, error handling.
- **Documentation stays private.** The API guide and endpoint reference sit behind platform authentication, visible only to contracted clients. There’s no public OpenAPI spec and no interactive explorer.
- **No webhooks.** Real-time updates mean polling the API yourself. There’s no event-driven or push-notification pattern. Scheduled delivery is what the Data Feed handles, not the API.
- **A sandbox does exist.** Once you’re in the process, PitchBook provides a test environment for practicing call structure before going live. The Direct Data team supports onboarding during this phase.

The PitchBook MCP server is an implementation of the Model Context Protocol that connects your AI agent and assistants like Claude, Cursor, etc directly to your PitchBook account. It provides structured and secure access to private-market data on companies, deals, funds, investors, people, and service providers, so your agent can research companies, analyze investors and financing activity, track company updates, and retrieve reports or profile files on your behalf.
- **Company research:** Have your agent retrieve company profiles, industries, active investors, deals, recent financing, debt financing, service providers, social analytics, and recent profile updates.
- **Investor and fund analysis:** Let the agent review investor profiles, investment preferences, funds, active investments, limited partner commitments, and target allocations.
- **People and service provider research:** Direct your agent to gather biographies, locations, team members, affiliates, and service provider details across multiple PitchBook entities.
- **Private-market news and documents:** Instruct your agent to retrieve credit news, download credit research, save entity profiles as PDFs, and download patent or news attachments.
- **Usage monitoring:** Have your agent check the connected PitchBook account's current and remaining daily limits before running research tasks.

Claude can show **Couldn't reach the MCP server** or **Authorization with the MCP server failed** when you add the connector for PitchBook.

mcp.snippet:
`https://premium.mcp.pitchbook.com/mcp`
TransportStreamable HTTP
AuthenticationOAuth
## Setup
```bash
claude mcp add pitchbook --transport http https://premium.mcp.pitchbook.com/mcp
```
## Frequently asked questions
### What is the PitchBook remote MCP server?
The PitchBook remote MCP server is a hosted Model Context Protocol endpoint at https://premium.mcp.pitchbook.com/mcp, so AI assistants can connect to it without installing or running anything locally. PitchBook provides data on private and public capital markets, covering companies, investors, deals, and funds. Its Premium remote MCP server brings that intelligence into assistant workflows for sourcing, diligence, and market research.
### How do I connect to the PitchBook MCP server?
Add the endpoint https://premium.mcp.pitchbook.com/mcp to any MCP-compatible client such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or VS Code. The setup snippets on this page configure each client in one step.
### Does the PitchBook MCP server require authentication?
Yes. PitchBook uses OAuth: the first time you connect, your MCP client opens a browser window to sign in and authorize access, then reuses the credentials for future sessions.
### Which transport does the PitchBook MCP server use?
PitchBook exposes a Streamable HTTP endpoint, the current standard transport for the Model Context Protocol, supported by all major MCP clients.
